title: Policy preview simulator — wireframes & grooming notes
content:
Purpose and high-level problem

This doc captures early wireframes, interaction notes, and backlog grooming for a Policy Preview Simulator: a sandboxed UI in the Rollouts Console that lets engineers and PMs preview how a rollout + fallback policy will behave against synthetic or recorded traffic before they deploy it. Goal: reduce surprise incidents and make fallback policies inspectable and explainable.

Why this is different from existing rollout previews
- Not just traffic-split visualization — simulates temporal effects (latency spikes, transient errors).
- Computes heuristic estimates (blast radius, expected token-cost delta, downstream error amplification).
- Lets you compose cascading fallback chains (model variant -> region -> capacity tier) and see ordered execution steps.
- Timeline scrubbing + heatmap to observe metric evolution and policy triggers.

Primary user journeys
1) QA engineer: load a recorded hour of traffic, attach a proposed policy (canary 5% -> 20% -> fallback to small-quantized model if latency > 800ms for 3s), scrub the timeline to see which requests would have been routed where, and generate a short report to share with dev.
2) PM/Owner: run a quick simulation on synthetic traffic to compare A/B variants (Variant A uses batching aggressiveness 50ms, Variant B uses 150ms) and see differences in latency and per-token cost.
3) SRE: validate that automatic fallback triggers don't cause event storms (e.g., cascade into full capacity failover). Use failure blast-radius estimator to tune thresholds.

Wireframe/interaction sketches (text description)
- Top bar: selector for traffic source {synthetic | recorded | live-preview*} and date/time window (if recorded). Toggle: include KV/prefix cache state (on/off).
- Left column (policy composer, compact):
  - Policy name, description free text
  - Stage sequence panel (drag to reorder): each stage card has type (percent-split, model-variant, region-route, capacity-tier, circuit-breaker), condition triggers (latency, error-rate, token-cost), and fallback target.
  - Quick-add templates: canary-basic, step-rollout, canary-with-auto-fallback, reroute-on-err-50.
- Center column (simulation canvas):
  - Top: timeline scrubber with play/pause, speed control (x0.5/1/2/5). Hover shows time and percent of traffic.
  - Middle: stacked heatmap (rows = metric groups: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, tokens-per-request, cost-per-token). Heatmap colors reflect severity and a transparent overlay shows where policy conditions fired.
  - Below heatmap: per-stage trace strip showing per-request routing outcome (color-coded): success @primary, success@fallback, error, throttled. Clicking a stripe opens a sidebar with the event payload and decision stack.
- Right column (inspector & metrics):
  - Live KPIs for current scrub time: served-requests, avg-cost, expected-sla-violations, predicted-monthly-cost-delta if policy were active. Button: Export snapshot (json/csv) and Generate human-readable summary.
  - Small card: Failure blast radius estimator (shows estimate of active users impacted if stage X fails). Controls: sensitivity slider (low/med/high) affects conservativeness.

Key interactions and microcopy examples
- When adding a fallback rule: "If p95 latency > 800ms for 30s, route 100% of affected requests to quantized-4bit-small (fallback) until p95 < 500ms for 2m." Button: "Simulate now".
- When drag-reordering stages: toast: "Reorder saved to preview draft — this does not affect live traffic."
- When a condition is met during simulation: callout with animated chevrons: "Condition triggered: Stage 2 -> failing over to eu-west-1-route. 142 requests affected in this window." Link: "View affected request samples."

Data sources & privacy notes
- Recorded traffic: allow redaction rules (PII scrubber) before simulation. Default: mask textual user inputs and hashed user ids.
- Synthetic traffic presets: conversational, short-queries, heavy-long-context. Each preset contains distribution for tokens-per-request and sequence lengths.

Instrumentation & analytics events (proposed)
- rollouts.preview.run (preview_id, policy_id, user_id, traffic_source, duration_seconds, num_requests_simulated)
- rollouts.preview.stage_fired (preview_id, stage_index, trigger_type, affected_count)
- rollouts.preview.export (preview_id, format, request_samples_count)
- rollouts.preview.heatmap_inspected (preview_id, metric, time_window)
- UI events for template usage and drag reorders for product analytics.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Users can upload a recorded traffic file (JSONL) and run a preview of a composed policy against it.
- Timeline heatmap renders p50/p95 latency and error-rate and highlights policy-trigger regions.
- Clicking a heatmap cell surfaces sample request traces and the decision stack for that trace.
- Export snapshot and human-readable summary generation works and attaches to a preview id.
- Policy drafts in the simulator are separated from live rollout configs and require an explicit 'Apply to live' step (with audit log).

Backlog & grooming list (with approximate estimates and priorities)
1) ROLL-2012: Synthetic traffic presets + editor UI (3 sprint-days) [P0] — needed for demo and UX testing.
2) ROLL-2013: Recorded-traffic upload + PII redaction toggle (2 sprint-days) [P0].
3) ROLL-2015: Heatmap component with metric layers & scrubber (5 sprint-days) [P1].
4) ROLL-2016: Decision-stack inspector & request trace viewer (4 sprint-days) [P1].
5) ROLL-2020: Failure blast-radius estimator (heuristic service + UI) (3 sprint-days) [P2].
6) ROLL-2031: Export snapshot/summary generator + github action to store previews (2 sprint-days) [P1].
7) ROLL-2040: Access controls — who can run previews with live-traffic (security review) (5 sprint-days) [P0].
8) ROLL-2055: A/B variant compare mode — diff view of metrics + per-model cost delta (6 sprint-days) [P1].

Edge cases and open questions (for engineering + privacy)
- How to simulate KV/prefix-cache warm starts? Option: load KV snapshots (privacy risk) or approximate hits via sampled cache-hit rates.
- Recorded traffic may include long-running streaming requests — how to represent partial streams in the timeline? Proposed: treat stream as series of tokens with aggregate latency windows.
- Cost estimates vs. actual billing: simulation should provide conservative bounds and clear microcopy: "Estimated cost delta — simulated. Actual billing may differ."
- When multiple fallback stages match, ensure deterministic tie-breaking (suggest rule: earlier stage in sequence wins).

Design tradeoffs and rationale notes
- Full-fidelity simulation (replaying exact runtime scheduling, batching, KV state) is expensive and brittle. MVP uses event-driven simulation with stochastic batching approximations. We will note assumptions clearly in UI.
- Keep the composer compact — advanced composer hidden behind "advanced" toggle to avoid scaring new users.
- Prioritize explainability: decision-stack entries should be small, chronological, and link to the condition definition.

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
- 11/10: produce low-fidelity mockups based on wireframe descriptions here (assign to Marco).
- 11/18: whiteboard session with SRE/Applied ML to validate heuristics for blast-radius and cost estimator (invite Li, Priya).
- 12/02: spike for synthetic-traffic presets + example datasets for demo (Evan to lead).

Appendix: sample micro-scenarios to include in demo dataset (short descriptions)
- Scenario A: sudden regional latency spike in us-west. Expectation: canary expansion halts and regional failover triggers.
- Scenario B: backend model begins returning 5xx errors at 12:17:05 for 2m -> circuit breaker opens and routes to cheaper quantized fallback.
- Scenario C: increased tokens-per-request (long context) causes token-cost to double and triggers cost-based fallback in third stage.

Notes to reviewers
- This is an early draft focusing on interaction vocabulary and backlog sizing. Please annotate the Confluence spec with any missing telemetry fields or legal/privacy requirements.
- Particularly want feedback on: blast-radius heuristic conservativeness, acceptable defaults for synthetic presets, and whether the scrubber should allow request-level stepping.

-- End of notes --
